title: Adaptive Observability and Deferred Profiling Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the process, configuration, and operational runbook for Adaptive Observability (AO): a low-overhead, signal-driven approach to enabling deferred and targeted profiling of the serving runtime in production. AO is designed to reduce continuous profiling overhead by collecting detailed traces only when specific signals indicate increased risk to SLOs or suspected regressions.

Goals

- Minimize steady-state telemetry and CPU/GPU overhead (target < 0.5% CPU overhead for control-plane agents).
- Provide fast, reproducible capture of kernel & request-level traces when anomalies occur.
- Ensure profiling activation is safe across kernel versions and model variants.
- Integrate with existing post-incident analysis and benchmarking suites for regression triage.

When to use AO

- Tail-latency excursions (> 95th/99th SLO breach) lasting > 1 minute.
- Regressions detected by continuous fidelity checks (quality or token-cost anomalies).
- Reproducible but infrequent workload spikes that require transient sampling.
- Pre-rollout canaries when testing new kernel or scheduler patches.

Signal taxonomy and thresholds

We use three classes of signals to decide whether to activate deferred profiling:

1) SLO Signals
   - 95th latency > configured SLO * 1.3 for > 60s (configurable).
   - Error rate > 0.5% sustained for > 30s.

2) Resource Signals
   - GPU occupancy deviation > 20% relative to baseline for 2+ minutes.
   - Host-level thermal or watchdog interrupts (NVML alert).

3) Heuristic / Anomaly Signals
   - Sudden unexplained spike in kernel dispatch times (per-kernel p99 grows > 2x).
   - Evaluation harness signals: batch mismatch or KV cache miss-rate climb.

Default thresholds are set in AO controller config. Operators can tune per-cluster or per-scheduler profile.

Safety and compatibility requirements

- Profiling artifacts must be writeable to a detached artifact store (S3-compatible) under /ao-traces/<cluster>/<node>/<timestamp>. This avoids I/O contention on local SSDs.
- Kernel-level instrumentation must be gated behind an compatibility matrix: only enable kernel-level event types listed in the current node's kernel-compat bundle.
- Sampling collectors run in user-space sidecars (service name: telemetry-bridge) and must be limited to 256 MB RSS and 10% CPU by cgroup.
- Any automatic activation must include an automated grace period of 30s; manual override available.

Implementation components

- AO Controller (service: ao-controller)
  - Receives aggregated signals from telemetry-bridge and slo-aggregator.
  - Applies policy rules (selectors, thresholds, cooldowns).
  - Issues activation requests to node-sidecar agents via gRPC.

- Node-sidecar (service: telemetry-bridge)
  - Runs on every runtime node as a DaemonSet.
  - Accepts activation token, spawns sampling process (perf/tracepoint/proxy-hooks), streams compressed trace to artifact store.
  - Publishes activation metadata to tracing-index (for later correlated queries).

- Tracing Index (service: trace-index)
  - Stores metadata records (JSON) for each trace: node, kernel-version, model-variant, request-filter, reason, associated alert ID.
  - Indexes by time, node, and correlation-id.

Policy examples

Default AO policy (yaml-like pseudoconfig)

  name: default-ao-policy
  match: cluster:prod, model_tier:hosted
  triggers:
    - signal: slo.latency.p95
      threshold: 1.3
      window_seconds: 60
    - signal: kernel.dispatch.p99
      threshold: 2.0
      window_seconds: 120
  sampling:
    duration_seconds: 300
    sampling_mode: stratified
    max_parallel_traces: 4
  safeguards:
    cooldown_seconds: 900
    max_activation_per_node_per_day: 6

Sampling modes

- ad-hoc: capture a single full trace for a specific request (highest fidelity).
- stratified: capture N traces covering short/long sequences and small/large batches.
- statistical: lower-fidelity counters + micro-profiles (lower overhead).

Runbook: immediate incident response (AO-driven capture)

1) Alerting and Triage
   - NOC or oncall receives p95/p99 alert from slo-aggregator with alert ID.
   - If alert matches AO policy (controller decision), ao-controller will auto-request a capture and post the activation to the incident channel.

2) Confirm activation
   - Oncall verifies activation metadata in trace-index and confirms that the node-sidecars have started streaming (check telemetry-bridge logs).
   - Command to check activation: curl -s http://ao-controller.local/api/v1/activations/<alert_id> | jq

3) Observe traces and preserve context
   - While traces are streaming, tag the incident (add correlation-id) and snapshot relevant runtime config (kernel hash, scheduler revision, model-variant tag).
   - If traces indicate sensitive customer data in payloads, immediately escalate to security and mark trace artifacts as restricted.

4) If no traces arrive
   - Verify agent health: kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=telemetry-bridge -o wide
   - Inspect controller logs: kubectl -n runtime logs deployment/ao-controller -c controller | tail -n 200
   - If agents are crashed or OOM-killed, follow node remediation runbook (see Related pages).

5) De-escalation
   - If activation captured sufficient traces and SLOs recover, allow sampling to stop automatically or trigger manual stop via ao-controller.
   - If activation causes instability (rare), use the ao-controller emergency-disable flag to stop further activations globally.

Post-incident analysis checklist

- Export trace bundle and store under incident artifact path.
- Run kernel-level diff against baseline (kernel-compat-report) and attach results to postmortem.
- Compare traces to benchmarking suite replay for the same workload signature. Note any divergence in scheduling decisions.
- If a kernel or scheduler bug is suspected, create a repo ticket with: trace-id, node image, kernel-version, scheduler revision, and a minimal repro steps.

Operational metrics to watch

| Metric | Target | Alert condition | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| AO activation overhead (control-plane CPU) | <0.5% | > 1% sustained | infra-observability |
| Successful trace uploads / activation | 99% | < 95% over a day | runtime-ops |
| Activation-induced node instability | 0 (baseline) | any OOM/Crash attributable to activation | sres |

Telemetry retention and access control

- All AO traces are retained 90 days in the artifact store by default. Longer retention is available for high-severity incidents via the incident workflow.
- Traces are tagged with confidentiality: internal or restricted. Restricted traces require approval from security to download.

Testing and rollout guidance

- Canary rollout matrix:
  - Stage 1: internal dev cluster, enable stratified sampling in manual mode for 48 hours.
  - Stage 2: staging cluster, enable auto-activation with conservative thresholds for 7 days.
  - Stage 3: prod small cohort (1/10 nodes), monitor activation overhead and upload success for 14 days.
  - Stage 4: gradual scale to full cluster with 24h burn-in windows.

- Use the benchmarking harness (workload-replay tool) to simulate activation patterns and validate trace fidelity vs. baseline.

Ownership and escalation

- AO Controller: runtime-infra team (owner: runtime-infra@redwood.ai)
- Node-sidecar / telemetry-bridge: observability team (owner: observability@redwood.ai)
- Artifact store and retention policy: platform-storage (owner: storage@redwood.ai)
- Security escalation: security@redwood.ai

Appendix A: Example diagnostic commands

- Check controller status:
  kubectl -n runtime get deployment ao-controller
  kubectl -n runtime logs deployment/ao-controller -c controller | grep activation

- List recent activations:
  curl -s http://trace-index.local/api/v1/activations?cluster=prod | jq .items | less

- Download a trace (requires appropriate RBAC):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ao-traces/prod/node-3/2026-02-28-09-21-33/trace.tar.gz ./

Appendix B: Minimal policy tuning matrix

- For high-throughput low-latency models (p95 < 100ms): lower sensitivity to p95 breaches, prefer statistical sampling.
- For long-sequence generators (avg tokens > 512): increase stratified sample duration to capture tail decoding behaviour.
